questions_and_answers.question_text: What does the use of shi bu shi qù imply, rather than qù bu qù?
Would qù bu qù also be correct?
What are the two ways to indicate destination?
Are the two forms equally used?
What does shàng mean in this exchange?
Write the Chinese question meaning "Does this bus go to Xīméndīng?"

answers.answer_text: Zhèibān chē shi bu shi qù Xīméndīng?

questions_and_answers.question_text: What did shàng mean in the Directions Module?

answers.answer_text: "To go up" — as in Shàng lóu.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Where does the destination come in relation to the main verb qù?

answers.answer_text: It directly follows the main verb.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Give both Chinese forms for "I am going to Xīméndīng."

answers.answer_text: Wǒ dào Xīméndīng qù, and Wǒ qù Xīméndīng.

articles.text:
6. D: Zhèibān chē shi bu shi qù      Does this bus go to Xīméndīng?
      Xīméndīng?
   E: Shì. Shàng chē ba!              Yes. Get on!

Notes on No. 6

Shi bu shi qù, "does it go to": The use of shi bu shi qù rather than qù bu qù in this sentence implies that the speaker has an idea that the bus does go to Xīméndīng and wants to make sure. (Zhèibān chē qù bu qù Xīméndīng? would also be correct.)

Qù Xīméndīng, "go to Xīméndīng": The destination directly follows the main verb qù. You now know two ways to indicate destination:

Wǒ dào Xīméndīng qù.             I am going to Xīméndīng.
Wǒ qù Xīméndīng.

The two forms are equally widely used.

Shàng chē: This verb has several meanings. In the Directions Module, the meaning was "to go up" in Shàng lóu, yòubian jiù shi mài dìtúde. In this exchange, the meaning of shàng is "to get on/in (a vehicle)."
